definition: An externally visible unit of application behavior that a component, function, process or interaction makes available to consumers (users, business processes, or other components) as a named set of operations, defined by what it offers rather than how it is implemented or accessed.

distinguish_from.when: the behavior is internal to a component, such as a private helper, mapper or validation routine, and is not offered as a named capability to callers outside that component
the symbol is the access point or binding through which a service is reached, such as an HTTP controller, gRPC endpoint, WebSocket handler or message listener, carrying a specific protocol
the symbol is the deployable or replaceable structural unit (module, package, microservice, class as a unit of deployment) that performs or realizes behavior, rather than the behavior it exposes
the symbol is an ordered sequence of steps, such as a saga, workflow or orchestrator method, that achieves a result rather than an offered capability

code_evidence: A service interface or abstract contract, such as IOrderService or a gRPC 'service' block in a .proto file, whose operations are injected into or called from controllers, handlers or other modules
A class annotated @Service, @Injectable or registered in a DI container whose public methods are invoked across module or component boundaries rather than only within its own package

A queue consumer, scheduled batch job or event subscriber documented or configured to fulfil requests from other systems under a named capability, for example a 'payment-processing' worker bound in messaging or cron configuration

attribute_descriptions.name: documentation
attribute_descriptions.description: Free-text description of what the service offers to its consumers, including its main operations and intended callers; set it whenever the service name alone does not convey its scope.

notes: In code, a @Service class is often both component and service. Classifiers need a rule: model the exposed contract as service and the deployable unit as component. serviceType mixes timing (synchronous/asynchronous) with style (event-driven/batch), so the values overlap. 'applicationinterface depends-on applicationservice' duplicates 'serves' and should be reviewed.
